tickets.title: Tapered nonuniform flow: close the global 945 candidate
tickets.first_deliverable: Correct the frontier flow types and actual half-port/cohort contracts, then prove a signed native-prefix rank profile and instantiate the outsider induction on the actual routed execution; see UB-22 through UB-24.
tickets.notes: 945 remains a conditional price, accepted best 1419. Recovery audit found that actual/reference size, total/half up-flow, cohort support, and frontier/interior occupancy must be distinguished. Exact whole-bag sorting for a<=2^60 fits within 1890 layers and can replace the complicated small-size provider. Whole-subtree and uniform ancestor bounds do not close the rank gate; a signed nonuniform profile is needed.

tickets.title: Compile the 2024 shallow high-arity k-sorters into binary sorters
tickets.first_deliverable: Identify a useful s-sorted/merge contract and prove its binary repair bridge; reopen numerical compilation only if a full binary depth calculation beats the tapered candidate.
tickets.notes: Existing k-sorting-2024 source screen: independent binary compilation with current base sorters does not improve the endpoint. Retain the localized-disorder interface as a research lead, not a projected sub-200 construction. See roadmap-700-200.md.

tickets.title: Screen feasible finite M before extracting the M-sorter constant
tickets.first_deliverable: Use the actual finite separator/geometry/fringe conditions to find feasible M, then extract c_M and charge binary replacement. The cited proof has necessary M >=204800, already excluding M=16/32.
tickets.notes: Source audit 2026-10-13: Theorem 1.2 uses M/32 < m <= M/16 and sqrt(2(1+ln m)/m) <= (1/5)*k^(-4). For k>=2 and integer m>=1 this implies m>=12800, hence M>=204800; the real finite threshold is larger. This is a necessary-condition hand derivation, not an improved upper bound. Do not substitute the large-M asymptotic coefficient at small M.

tickets.notes: Chvatal DCS-TR-294 s.9, Seiferas s.7: Komlos 'around 60 to 100'; all sources unverified, no parameters given.

tickets.title: Run-aware first column sort (skip merge levels using sorted input runs)
tickets.first_deliverable: Chunk invariant and inter-stage permutation Pi_t, then switch big nodes to physicalPackNetBlock
tickets.notes: Components proved in Lean (kernel-checked, experiments/runaware): block-merge column sorter (physicalPackNetBlock_exec/_depth_le), 2^29 divisibility of runs (NodeGeomD), GenNetwork stage composition (stages_sort). Payoff -12% at m~2^58 but only ~3% at the two-round window m~2^42.

tickets.title: Replace the tapered final column sort by a certified promised repair
tickets.first_deliverable: Specify the repair network and prove its deterministic cut bound against the full-sort baseline plus explicit tail mass; then prove one uniform scramble witness for all consumed cuts/ranks, both orientations, padding and fringe cohorts. Reprice the entire final operation against <=140 layers under the intended 945 schedule.
tickets.notes: Rebased 2026-10-13: retaining two depth-630 sorts gives coefficient (1260+R)/2 if the tapered global schedule closes. R=200 prices to730; R=140 to700; R=136 to698. These are arithmetic gates, not constructed repairs. Existing RMS/sampled displacement does not supply uniform adversarial tails; L1 alone permits a profile about 40x over the desired cut allowance. See UB-18 and roadmap-700-200.md. Earlier unverified samples at m=4096,n=256 reported RMS displacement about 3*m^(1/4) and adversarial maximum about 115; these are discovery data. The earlier 1050 projection used the 1419 schedule.

tickets.title: Reduce the fringe floor (f below 2^17) for the two-round node
tickets.first_deliverable: Audit a small-fringe contract at arbitrary column width, including the nonempty large-rank R2n event, and charge the same network bulk/fringe failure budget. Distinguish it from the already present width-16 provider.
tickets.notes: Observed 2026-10-13: tapered-945 CyclicSmallF2Params/AdaptivePaddedWitness use f=16000 at width 16 and common rare-rank coefficient 1/9000000. Its R2n range is empty, so this is not a general-width small-fringe theorem. The standard large-width branch retains f=131040. Lowering the scale further must reprice both probability and flow conditions.

tickets.title: Extract the minimal tapered cut/rank provider contract
tickets.first_deliverable: Map every ordinary/frontier badSend0 and fringeSend use to positional cuts and native rank thresholds; prove a sufficient prescribed-cut interface or document why all-cut control is necessary.
tickets.notes: AdaptivePaddedWitness currently quantifies over every r<=a. A 65-cut gadget is not a substitute. Cut choices must depend only on fixed schedule geometry, never the input. Enables a correctly scoped UB-14 search.

tickets.title: Track signed cumulative cut discrepancy in the multiway transfer
tickets.first_deliverable: Derive a finite affine transfer for signed cut discrepancies, child-count defects, left/right outsider imbalance and higher-rank errors; close forcing, root/frontier and terminal-purity budgets with explicit depth.
tickets.notes: Information retained by this state may sharpen current per-child bounds. It does not erase the approximately 32 mismatches per outsider in the one-sided 64-child example. Keep every such amplification in the operator. No contraction or coefficient is claimed.

tickets.title: Add adjacent-region compaction and attenuation as a repair channel
tickets.first_deliverable: Prove or refute a fixed even/odd adjacent-region repair family with compaction/attenuation, simultaneous threshold guarantees, far-jump leakage and a complete composable depth recurrence.
tickets.notes: A new lateral comparison channel could bypass the old assumption that all repair passes through parent fringe bandwidth. No adjacent-only per-key error premise is established. Charge compaction and every serial layer; input-dependent maximum matchings are not comparator networks. For a new factor-64 macro-stage, total depth gates are 4200 for 700 and 1200 for 200.

tickets.title: Audit tapered obstructions and specify first sub-1000 recovery gates

tickets.notes: Completed source audit and recovery plan with two read-only sub-agent reviews and exact-rational calculations. No Lean rebuild or new sorting theorem. Implementation gates are UB-22, UB-23 and UB-24; the tapered worktree was not modified.

tickets.title: Use exact small-bag sorters and correct the large ordinary provider contract
tickets.first_deliverable: Prove an exact local provider for all a<=2^60 with depth<=1830 and actual half-up cohort support. For larger ordinary bags, prove one narrow-row rectangle and both half-fringe fit and cohort range; screen mu_new=63/64 times the old mu.
tickets.notes: Existing bitonic depth source makes exact small bags affordable under the 1890 ceiling. Candidate large ordinary screen uses M=2^34+2^28 and arbitrary integer column count; positive scalar/support margins are model evidence only. Frontier providers still use their own count/port shapes.

tickets.title: Give every tapered frontier its own flow and discrepancy target
tickets.first_deliverable: Replace the all-active ordinary LocalIntegerFlow wrapper by a shape-indexed family; prove receiver counts and conservation through bootstrap, a symbolic six-stage cycle, and meeting.
tickets.notes: Current GlobalFlowStep assumes frontier counts near ordinary mass, incompatible with FrontierDebtFlow top/bottom targets. At e=0 the top discrepancy is C/2^24, not a bounded rounding error. SameBagScale selects top-frontier bags, not strict interior bags.

tickets.title: Prove the signed native-prefix rank profile before extending the outsider induction
tickets.first_deliverable: Prove the clipped prefix-count identity and the exact bootstrap profile; close a symbolic six-stage ordinary/frontier rank recurrence with native-prefix cancellation, cohort errors and a valid upper-retirement rule.
tickets.notes: Ancestor/fringe keys are intentionally concentrated near descendant endpoints. Descendant-only deficits have signed q_j terms; their cancellation needs an ancestor lower bound in the same prefix. Keep shared endpoint deficits until telescoping; reject uniform ancestor-share assumptions. No global stability theorem is claimed.

tickets.title: Preserve sorted packets using merge-and-deal balancing throughout the scheduler
tickets.first_deliverable: Prove the exact merge-and-deal threshold-count identity; certify one matching-cycle family and bulk/tail bounds at unbounded packet counts; trace sorted packets through a complete ordinary/frontier routing cycle and price repacking.
tickets.notes: Author/signature: GPT-6 (Codex), 2026-10-14; exact runtime variant/effort not exposed. Merging two sorted 2^q packets and dealing alternate outputs implements rounded averaging in q+1 layers. Conditional deterministic L2 screen avoids a profile union, but rare cohorts and packet-preserving global routing are open. The q=12, 30-round, coefficient-195 calculation is only a depth gate under an unchanged stage rate; no matching/tail tuple is claimed. Extends UB-13 by changing the mixing operation, not just the first sort.

tickets.title: Bootstrap a binary power-scale localization network through recursive overlapping cleanup
tickets.first_deliverable: Screen and close the early-stop Chvatal route using the stranger-tail width and actual wire geometry; identify a binary multiscale rank-pure prefix with depth coefficient p < 200*(1-theta), or a concrete obstruction, for blocks of size n^theta.
tickets.notes: Claimed 2026-10-14 by Codex (GPT-6), branch ub-26-localization. A rank-pure block partition gives one parallel recursive cleanup and coefficient p/(1-theta); an s-sorted interval of width n^theta uses two overlapping cleanup passes and coefficient a/(1-2*theta). The checked Chvatal proof gets rank purity only at fixed 2^42-wire blocks. A rough stranger-tail exponent screen shows its optimistic early-stop/window-cleanup price exceeds 1419 for every positive stop fraction; physical wire localization is still unproved. No cheaper prefix is identified yet.

tickets.title: Alternate coarse stages with periodic precision restoration and certify the whole period
tickets.first_deliverable: Screen an ideal exact-bag restoration stage after coarse routing on actual ports; if recoverable, derive a phase-indexed affine error transfer including forcing, transient cohort support, frontiers, terminal purity and actual bits advanced per period.
tickets.notes: Author/signature: GPT-6 (Codex), 2026-10-14. Changes precision over time, beyond UB-19's static weighted profile. At the unchanged tapered stage rate, seven hypothetical depth-64 stages plus one depth-1890 restoration price to 146.125; no coarse provider or valid cycle is known. Local exact sorting cannot recover keys absent from the bag. Reject cycles that lose repair reach or stall advancement; reusing tapered flow requires UB-23/24's actual rank accounting.

tickets.title: Certify a whole randomized multiscale network using paired Boolean forcing witnesses
tickets.first_deliverable: Define a dyadic even/odd block-pair matching family; extract compatible output-1/output-0 forcing certificates and compare with exhaustive or SAT failures; derive or refute a uniform witness-counting recurrence before seeking a whole-run failure bound below one.
tickets.notes: Author/signature: GPT-6 (Codex), 2026-10-14. Explore one global existence proof instead of universally good local gadgets. At AND/OR comparator gates, a surviving adjacent inversion has disjoint initial 1- and 0-forcing leaf sets; counting must preserve shared DAG dependencies. The candidate two-pass d-matching schedule has depth gate 2d<200 before extra sweeps. Per-input high probability from Randomized Shellsort does not imply one network works for all inputs; no successful counting estimate or sorter is claimed.
